why: Every sheet must be mapped, in scope or out of it. Leaving the rate-and-revenue sheet out is reported as a gap for a human, which wastes their time on a decision policy has already made - out of scope is a decision, not a gap (D-SCOPE-02). The out-of-scope metrics are the three rows the 'Rate & Revenue' sheet actually carries: average daily rate, RevPAR and average length of stay. This case listed `revenue` instead until the first real recording disagreed with it - `policy.yaml` has both names in its out-of-scope vocabulary and the workbook has only one of them, so a hand-written expectation could name the wrong one and look right.
